identity.title: NeuralPlane: Structured 3D Reconstruction in Planar Primitives with Neural Fields

problem.claim: Reconstruct multi-view 3D scenes as compact, semantically aligned planar primitives using neural fields.

contributions.claim: NeuralPlane distills inconsistent 2D plane observations into a unified 3D neural representation.
The approach combines monocular plane-observation generation with plane-guided training for implicit 3D geometry learning.
A self-supervised Neural Coplanarity Field models scene semantics alongside geometry.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents a neural-field approach specifically for multi-view 3D plane reconstruction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report high-fidelity reconstructions with crisp planar primitives aligned with semantic content, without prior plane annotations.
The authors report that experiments on ScanNetv2 and ScanNet++ demonstrate superiority in both geometry and semantics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Planar primitives are presented as compact and expressive representations for man-made environments.
NeuralPlane applies neural fields to multi-view 3D plane reconstruction.
The method unifies inconsistent 2D plane observations by distilling geometric and semantic cues into a 3D neural representation.
Its components generate monocular plane observations, learn geometry through plane-guided training, and model semantics with a self-supervised feature field.
The authors report annotation-free, high-fidelity reconstruction and superiority on ScanNetv2 and ScanNet++.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links each major design component to a distinct target: observations, geometry, or semantics, then reports results for geometry and semantics.

lessons.interpretation: This creates a visible correspondence between method components and evaluation dimensions.
lessons.application: When presenting a multi-component method, map each component to an explicit capability and evaluate those capabilities separately.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when components are inseparable or the evaluation cannot isolate their intended roles.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation metrics, baselines, quantitative gains, or experimental conditions behind the reported superiority.
It does not state a limitation of existing approaches or establish priority beyond the authors' stated description of NeuralPlane.
